paper.title_en: On-demand frequency-entangled microwave biphotons from a transmon-resonator dimer
paper.abstract_en: We propose a superconducting circuit QED source of on-demand frequency-entangled microwave photon pairs, with one photon emitted into each of two separate waveguides, enabling individual manipulation. The design is based on a transmon-resonator dimer, which consists of two transmon-resonator subsystems coupled through a cross-Kerr interaction. We outline a viable circuit-QED realization in which the required cross-Kerr interaction is implemented using Josephson-junction couplers. To analyze the emission dynamics, we derive and numerically solve the set of evolution equations that enable tracking the evolution of the joint spectral intensity of photons. We characterize the resulting photon-number correlations, frequency anticorrelation, and spectral entanglement. By varying the coupling strengths, we obtain biphotons with distinct joint spectral intensities and Schmidt spectra, ranging from broadly distributed multimode entanglement to states dominated by two nearly equally weighted Schmidt contributions. In the latter regime, optimizing the transmon-resonator coupling and detuning yields an output biphoton state that has fidelity $F \approx 0.956$ with a two-dimensional maximally entangled state. Restricting the local target modes to separated frequency bins yields a fidelity $F_\mathrm{bin} \approx 0.949$, indicating that the output state closely approximates a frequency-bin Bell pair. Thus, the proposed microwave biphoton source provides a route toward distributing frequency-encoded quantum resources between remote superconducting nodes.
